newsitem.title: UK: Scrap vehicle tax on sub-1500 CC cars - UK Lords.
newsitem.headline: Scrap vehicle tax on sub-1500 CC cars - UK Lords.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke should scrap vehicle excise duty on cars and vans with engines of under 1500 cc as part of a drive to reduce air pollution and fuel consumption, the House of Lords Select Committee on Science and Technology said on Wednesday.
It said the 1.4 billion pound cost of the measure could be recouped through higher duties on petrol and diesel.
In a report entitled "Towards Zero Emissions for Road Transport", the committee also proposed taxing "green" fuels such as natural gas and liquid petroleum gas at a lower rate.
It also recommended that the duty on fuels with very low sulphur contents should also be reduced, and their use be made compulsory by the year 2000.

Government departments and local authorities should take the lead by converting their fleets to gas or electric vehicles, and financial incentives should be offered to other fleet operators to make the same switch, the all-party committee of parliament's upper chamber said.

"Taken together, our package of recommendations are a blueprint for reducing the environmental impact of road vehicles without destroying the immense benefits they have brought," said Lord Robert Dixon-Smith, the Conservative chairman of the panel.
